# read_C: pp. 96–98 (leaves n97–n99), plus the seam line 95.5 and the opening of p. 99 (n100), read from the images

## Lines, layout, and where the part ends

- p. 96 (n97) has five lines. It is a leaf back with no ornament. Line slope is near zero. Headlines are at about 120, 175, 232, 288 and 343. The inner right frame is at x≈1815.
- p. 97 (n98) has five lines. It is a leaf front and opens with the horizontal swirl, then `༔`, a wide blank, and `༔`. I wrote it `༄༅༔ ༔`, following the editor's 009 decision. The leaf number is in the left margin.
  - The scan is rotated by about +2.8°, so I read it from a deskewed copy.
  - Headlines in the deskewed copy are at 146, 202, 262, 318 and 374.
- p. 98 (n99) has five lines. It is a leaf back with no ornament. The scan is rotated by about −1.8°, so I read it deskewed. Headlines are at 116, 172, 230, 284 and 336.
- p. 99 (n100) is a leaf front and opens `༄༅༔ ༔`. Its first words are `ནས་བོས་ལ་འདི་སྐད་དོ༔ ཀྱེ་རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ …`. I read only that far.
- In all I read 15 print lines, plus the seam line 95.5 and the first words of 99.1.

**Start (seam with B).** Line 95.5 (n96), as I read it: `…ཀྱི་སྐུ་ལ་འཁྲིལ་བ༔ གཡས་པས་མགུལ་ནས་འཁྱུད་ཅིང༔ གཡོན་པས་དུང་དམར་ཞལ་དུ་སྟོབ་[filler dots]པ༔ རང་གི་ཀླད་པའི་ནང་གི་ལྷོ་ནས་ཐོན་ནས་རང་ལ་`.
- 95.5 ends `རང་ལ་` with a tsheg, and p. 96 opens `འཆར་དུ་འོང་བས`. So the seam reads `…ཐོན་ནས་རང་ལ་འཆར་དུ་འོང་བས་དེ་ལ…`, which is clean.
- The filler dots inside `སྟོབ་…པ` are left out, as at 87.2.

**END: proposed at 98.3, after `…ཐིམ་ནས|སངས་རྒྱས་པར་འགྱུར་རོ༔`** (x≈590 on the deskewed n99 line 3, about a third of the way along the line).
- This `རོ༔` closes the whole eleventh-day (Padma Heruka) section, and it is a true sentence end.
- The next words, `ཡང་དེ་ལྟར་ངོ་སྤྲད་ཀྱང་བག་ཆགས་ངན་པས…`, begin the twelfth day (Karma Heruka and the gaurīs, etc.). That is the natural opening of part 011.
- No sentence closes after it on p. 98:
  - 98.4 `…ཡོད་པས༔` and 98.5 `…འོང་སྟེ༔`, `…འོངས་པས༔` and `ངོ་སྤྲད་པ་ནི༔` are all clause links.
  - The next true sentence end is `…ཡང་ཚེ་འདས་ཀྱི་མིང|ནས་བོས་ལ་འདི་སྐད་དོ༔` on 99.1, at x≈850. That is only a speech-introduction formula, and it would split the twelfth-day passage.
- **The fallback is to finish on 99.1 at `…འདི་སྐད་དོ༔`.** If the editor wants every line of p. 98 in this part, that is the place: the rest of 98.3 to 98.5, plus 99.1 up to `དོ༔`.
- Under my proposal, part 010 is pp. 90.2–98.3, and **part 011 begins on 98.3 with `ཡང་དེ་ལྟར་ངོ་སྤྲད་ཀྱང…`**.
- I still transcribed 98.3 (rest), 98.4 and 98.5 in full in read_C.txt, so the editor can choose.

**Proposed `# name:`** `The blood-drinkers of days eight to eleven`. Alternatives are `Buddha, Vajra, Ratna and Padma Heruka`, or `The first four Herukas`.
- Part 010 holds the closing praise of the text (90.2 onward) and the introduction to the wrathful bardo.
- It then gives the Herukas of the eighth day (Buddha), ninth (Vajra), tenth (Ratna) and eleventh (Padma), with the instruction to recognise each.
- If the fallback end is taken, the name still fits, because only the twelfth day's first lines are added.

## Method

- I found the line bands from row profiles. For n98 and n99 I first found the skew by maximising row-profile variance (+2.8° and −1.8°) and cropped a rotated copy.
- Each line was cropped in three or four overlapping segments at ×2.4–×2.6. Doubtful syllables were cropped at ×5–×12 (LANCZOS).
- I made side-by-side montages for letter shapes: the khrag stacks; ངོ against ངོ་ཤེས on 98.1–2; and the ending of 98.4.
- Mid-line tshegs are mostly fused to the head bars in this print. Where the image cannot decide, I followed normal syllable division.
- I checked line-end tshegs at ×7–×12.

I see no `འུ` after it: the next thing is a tsheg and then `ཆུང`. So the print appears to have `རྔེ་ཆུང` (or a cramped `རྔེའུ`). I took the stack as རྔེ because it fits the witness and the traces. |
| 98.2 | `ཡིན་པར་ངོ[?]་ཤེས་ནས` | After `པར` comes a ང with no visible naro. The long e-stroke of the following ཤེ starts right over it, so a naro may be merged into it or broken. "ངོ་ཤེས" is the only sense ("recognising [him] as the yidam deity"), and 98.1 has a clear `ངོ་ཤེས`. If the editor holds that no naro is printed, this becomes a misprint `ང་ཤེས → ངོ་ཤེས`. |

There are no `[…]` gaps.

## Where the other recension differs in sense (print followed)

- **96.4:** print "through the power of bad habits [he] is frightened and flees **back**", where the other recension has "**is dragged back** by bad habits". Print `ངོ་མ་འཕྲོད་ན` ("if he does not meet [them]") is conditional where the witness is causal (`པས`).
- **96.5:** the print says "the **deity host** of the Padma family of blood-drinkers comes to meet him" (`ལྷ་ཚོགས`). The other recension names only the family.
- **96.5–97.1:** the print omits `མ་ཡེངས་པར་ཉོན་ཅིག` ("listen without distraction") in the call to the deceased.
- **97.2:** the print adds `ཞལ` ("face") and says the centre face is "**blazing** dark red" (`དམར་ནག་ཏུ་འབར་བ`).
- **97.3:** the print specifies the consort embraces "the **father's** body" (`ཡབ་ཀྱི་སྐུ`). The wording matches days 9–10 in the witness.
- **97.3:** `རྔེ[?]་ཆུང`, the small drum, where the witness has `རྔེའུ་ཆུང`. The sense is the same.
- **97.4–5:** the print has "from the **west** of the brain" without "inside" (`ནང་གི`). It has "emerges and comes" (`ཐོན་ནས་འོང་བས`) and lacks "shines upon you" (`རང་ལ་འཆར་དུ`).
- **97.5: "meditate on joy" (`དགའ་བ་བསྒོམ་ཤིག`)**, where the other recension has "arouse mindfulness" (`དྲན་པ་བསྐྱེད་ཅིག`). **This is a real sense difference.**
- **98.1:** `རང་གི་ཡི་དམ` ("your own yidam") without `ཁྱོད`, and no second "do not be scared". The sense is the same.
- **98.2:** print `ཡི་དམ་གྱི་ལྷ་ཡིན་པར་ངོ་ཤེས` ("recognising [him] **as** the yidam deity"), where the witness has "since he is the yidam, recognising". The sense is close.
- **98.3–4:** print "…flees and does **not recognise** the yidam, and **there are those who** do not meet it" (`ངོ་མ་ཤེས་ཏེ་མ་འཕྲོད་པ་ཡོད་པས`). The other recension has "it is **possible** not to meet it" (`ངོ་མ་འཕྲོད་པ་སྲིད་པས`).
- **98.4–5:** the list of escorts in the print is "the deity host of the Karma-family blood-drinkers, the Gaurīs, the Phra men, the **sme ma**, and the Īśvarīs". **The print adds `སྨེ་མ`**, and it has `ཕྲ་མེན` without `མ`. See the misprints.
- **98.5:** print "not recognising them, **the terror grows greater**" (`འཇིགས་སྐྲག་ཆེ་རུ་འོངས་པས`), where the witness has "he will be frightened" (`སྐྲག་ཏུ་འོང་བས`).

## Suspected misprints

1. **98.2 `ངོ[?]་ཤེས`.** If the naro is truly absent, it is a misprint for `ངོ་ཤེས`. Only that sense works. Moderate certainty. See the [?] entry.
2. **98.4–5 `ཕྲ་མེན་དང༔ སྨེ་མ་དང༔`.** The witness has the single item `ཕྲ་མེན་མ་དང༔`. The print may have split `ཕྲ་མེན་མ` / `ཕྲ་སྨེན་མ` into two items, or it may genuinely list an extra class. **I cannot decide which, so the passage is kept with a note only.**
3. **97.3 `རྔེ[?]་ཆུང`** for `རྔེའུ་ཆུང`. This is probably the print's abbreviation or spelling, so it is kept with a note only.
4. **96.1 and elsewhere: `དངངས` for `སྔངས`.** This is the print's consistent spelling (`dngangs` "terrified"), not a misprint. It is kept.
5. **98.5 `ཆེ་རུ`** ("grows greater"). It is an unusual idiom but makes sense, so it is kept.
